ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: planning ahead
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What the colony will run short of, worked out from the live game, and the one-click steps that would prevent it
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Start with the first suggestion: they are ordered by how soon something runs short. "Not this" sets one aside for good, until you bring it back.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: The top of the Making page (Planning, then Making) is the Ahead section: what the colony keeps a stock of and how long each lasts, the fields against the year, and suggestions for what to do about them, the soonest short first. Each suggestion shows its reason in numbers, and nothing happens until you click: Do it, Show (the view moves there and the cells are outlined), or Not this. Everything is worked out again each hour from what is on the map now and what the colony used over the last days, so a suggestion goes by itself once its reason is gone. The automations in the settings stay as they are, off unless you switch them on.

li.heading: What it reads
li.text: Who eats here: colonists and slaves, prisoners, Hospitality's guests (they eat the colony's meals), and the colony's animals fed from the stores (those that can't graze, and all of them while nothing grows). Each one's need comes from their own hunger, so genes, pregnancy and age count; a grown colonist needs 1.6 nutrition a day. What there is: everything stored or lying about and not forbidden, as the Making page reads it, with the storage cells each kind takes and the share kept frozen. What is used: the colony's record of the last 3 days (meals and food eaten, what the bills took, medicine, clothes worn through), kept through the deeper game hooks; until it covers a day, the use is estimated. What the land gives: each growing zone's crop at its own soil, and the year's warmth from the land's temperatures by twelfth.

li.heading: How the targets are worked out
li.text: Food is weighed by its nutrition and storage by its cells, never by the number of pieces: a big pile of a crop with little nutrition in each piece is a small stock. A target is a day's use times the days set in the settings (Building, Planning ahead), cut to what keeps before it rots and to the room in the stores.

table.li: Stock | A day | To keep
Meals | The hunger of everyone who eats here (or what the record shows, if more) | 2 days by default; without a freezer no more than half the days a meal keeps (2 for a simple meal)
Raw food | The cooks' need: a simple or fine meal takes 0.5 nutrition of ingredients for 0.9 | 5 days by default, plus the days nothing grows in the next 60
Animal feed | The hunger of the animals fed from the stores | As raw food
Medicine | The record, or one a day for each who needs tending and a tenth a head | 5 days by default
Spare clothes | Clothes worn through, by the record | 5 days by default
Materials | What the blueprints and frames still need | All of it

li.after: Short means under a day left, or under a quarter of the target; low, under three quarters; more than needed, over twice the target, with the storage cells it takes.

table.li: Suggestion | When | What it does

Raise a bill | Meals, medicine or feed are short or low and the bills ask for less than the target | Sets the biggest "do until" bill's count so the bills together cover the target, rounded up to fives
Add a bill | No bill makes them at all | Adds a "do until" bill at a bench here, and a bill for each of its parts that is short and that a bench here makes, as the chains below do
Copy to a second bench | The benches with the bill can't make a day's use with the hands there are | Copies the bill, with its count and ingredients, to another bench of that kind
Lower a bill | The meal bills ask for more than half again what keeps without a freezer, and the store is full | Lowers the biggest bill toward what keeps
Grow a field | The fields fall short of the year's need | Adds free fertile cells next to a food field, the best yield first, at most 80 a step
Switch a crop | The fields fall short and a crop's stock covers a year of its use | Sows a band at one end of that field with the best food crop instead
A new field | The fields still fall short | Lays out a field of the best food crop on free fertile ground near the fields

li.heading: Why it's stuck
li.text: A meal, medicine or feed bill behind a short or low stock that isn't moving gets a suggestion of its own saying why, in this order: it is suspended; its bench is forbidden, broken down, without power or out of fuel; the one it is kept for can't do it; nobody here can (the work, the skill it needs, the bill's skill range); nobody who can has the work switched on; none of its ingredients is in stock; they are, but outside the bill's radius; no store that takes the product has room. Where a fix exists it is one click: resume, allow the bench, let anyone do it, let the best colonist do the work (priority 3), the bill for a missing ingredient a bench here makes, or the whole map as the radius. A food field mostly unsown in the growing season gets the same: its sowing switched off, or nobody able to sow.

li.heading: The fields
li.text: The crop food the colony needs a day is the cooks' need for meals and the feed animals' need, less the share of raw food that came from meat by the record. A field gives its harvest's nutrition over the days it takes to grow at its soil (resting at night, from about 7 in the evening to 6 in the morning), on each day's warmth: a crop grows fully between its optimal temperatures (6 to 42 for most) and not at all below its least (0 for most). Over the next 60 days the fields must give what the colony eats in all of them, the days without growing included; the shortfall is covered in steps, and each step says how much food a day it adds. The line under the stocks gives the need, what the fields give, the growing days left this year and the days ahead with nothing growing. Hay and the other crops only animals eat are kept apart: they feed the animals fed from the stores and never count as the people's food, while what the people's fields give beyond the people's need feeds the animals too. A hay field is grown only for the animals, and a store of hay nobody eats can be switched to a food crop.

li.heading: Only suggestions
li.text: A step is done only when you click it, and it is told in a message. "Done lately" lists the last steps: each can be undone (a bill goes back to its old count or off its bench, a zone gives its new cells back, a priority goes back to what it was), and a while after it was done the council checks whether it worked: a bill step a day later (the stock rose a quarter of the way to its target, or the bench made half a day's use), a field step two days later (half its cells sown). If not, it is looked at once more, then it says what is in the way. A step waiting for its check isn't suggested again. "Not this" sets a suggestion aside until you bring it back from "Set aside"; its share goes to the next way, another field or another bill.

li.heading: Building ahead
li.text: The Plan page (Planning, then Plan) opens with Building ahead: the rooms the colony will be short of, worked out each hour from the map in the same way, and the next one or two rooms to build, the most urgent first. Each kind of room is weighed by what the colony needs against what is built and what is planned (blueprints, frames and rooms being built), and a room is suggested before it is short where that can be known: once the prisoners being recruited join, or once the winter's days without growing come. It only suggests: Place the blueprints puts the room down as the room planner would, with your materials and settings, at a spot the planner's "find a good spot" gives, beside the rooms it goes with (bedrooms together, the freezer and the dining room by the kitchen, workshop and store side by side, a hospital near the gate) and never over a field. Undo takes the blueprints and the marks to cut or mine away again; what was already built stays.

table.li: Room | Needed | Counted as built

Beds | Everyone who sleeps here (colonists, slaves, quest lodgers), the prisoners being recruited once they join, and the people an accepted quest brings to join once they come | Sleeping places in the colony's beds, not medical, not for prisoners or guests

Cold store | Places for a stack of the meals the stock target keeps and of the raw food for its days, then for the days without growing ahead; by the nutrition a place of the colony's own food holds as it lies in store | Places in stores in a room below zero, and in powered fridges (RimFridge's among them)
Seats | Everyone who eats here, Hospitality's guests too, and those who will join, less 1 (someone is always asleep or out) | Chairs beside an eating table
Hospital beds | 1 for every 4 people as a start, or as many as were laid up at once over the last 15 days if more | Medical beds, not for prisoners

Workshop | A place for every workshop bench, and one more beside a bench that is busy with no idle bench of its kind: by the record of the last days, worked 6 of a hand's 8 hours a day with as much work again waiting; until the record covers a day, more work that can go ahead waiting than its hands do in 2 days of 8 hours | Benches in a workshop, and a place for every 10 free cells of workshop floor
Stores | The stacks lying about at home that a store would take, 5 or more | Free places in the stores, the cold ones aside

li.after: Never more building is queued than the builders do in 2 days: a builder's day counts 6 hours of building at their construction speed, and a piece's work is doubled for fetching its materials and walking. Rock to mine for a room counts too, at the miners' pace: a swing of the pick every 100 ticks at a plain miner's speed, taking 80 hit points off natural rock, so the miners' days for it are counted in the builders' hours, both for a room still to place and for the rock marked inside the rooms being built. While more than that is queued, the next room waits and the page says so. Building ahead stays on the Plan page when the colony's next steps are switched off in the settings. "Not this" on a room sets that kind of room aside until you bring it back.

li.heading: Rooms in stages, and room to grow
li.text: A room placed from Building ahead, or by you with the room planner, is followed until it stands, stage by stage: clearing the ground, walls, doors and roof, cooling, heating and power, floors, furniture. With build priorities on, the stage at hand can be set to high, so the walls go up before the furniture; a material the site needs 40 or more of, with no store taking it within 14 cells, gets a stockpile made beside the site. What holds a room up is named with its fix where one exists: nobody with Construction (or plant cutting or mining for what is in the way) switched on, a roof nobody marked, too little skill, no way there, forbidden pieces, the materials short with how many, research, or the builders' other work. Two days after a room was placed the council checks that its walls stand or a third of it is built. Each room keeps one side free to grow into, the side with the most free ground beyond its wall and not its door's, 3 to 6 cells deep; the kept ground shows on the map while you place a building, a zone or a room, and a blueprint put down there gets a warning that can take it away again. The ground plan (Plan this, the whole base) finds its spots around the rooms being built and their kept sides too.

li.heading: Spare clothes
li.text: For each garment the colony's people wear, the council counts those worn below half their hit points (the game's frayed clothes, a mood penalty), those that will wear below half within the days set at the garment's own wear a day, and those the record saw worn through in as many days. When these outrun the whole spares in store and what the bills will still make, a suggestion keeps enough spares: it raises the garment's "do until" bill, or adds one at a bench here that can make it, counting only whole pieces (half their hit points or more), so worn ones in store don't stand in for spares. A bill Everybody Gets One sets for the garment is left alone; a garment no bench here makes goes on the shopping list instead. At most 3 garments are suggested at once, the most short first, and two days after a step the council checks that the bill made some.

li.heading: Colony Manager
li.text: With Colony Manager, its jobs show beside the stock rows: hunting, logging, mining and foraging with what each counts, what there is and the target it works to, and each herd with its animals against the count wanted. The council only reads them. When the colony wants more of what a job brings in than its target (meat for the raw food, by the share of meat the record saw eaten; wood for the blueprints, the chains and what the fires, stoves and bills used lately for the days set; the minerals on the shopping list), a suggestion raises the target, by tens up to 200 and by fifties above, never past the job's own slider; Undo puts it back, and two days later the council checks that the count rose a quarter of the way. A suspended job whose goods are wanted gets a suggestion to resume it. A manager that can't work at all is named first: no manager desk (and which desk can be built now), a desk without power, forbidden or broken down (a forbidden one is allowed at a click), or nobody with Managing switched on (the best colonist for it can be let do it, by intellectual and social skill). A working AI manager does the work by itself. Without the mod nothing of this shows.

li.heading: The shopping list, and where to mine
li.text: Under the fields comes what the colony wants and can't make here, for the next trader: the parts down a chain that no bench here makes and no field grows (steel for components, neutroamine for medicine), the materials the blueprints are short of, what a bill waits for that nothing here makes, components before Fabrication, medicine itself when no bench makes it, and clothes no bench here makes. Each reason is reckoned against the same stock, so they add up and the stock is counted once; what is already marked to mine comes off at the rock's yield. Each row gives how many are short, what there is against what is wanted, their worth in silver at the base price, and where they may come from. Crops, meat, hides, wool, milk, eggs, wood and stone chunks come from the land and never go on the list. A trader on the map or in orbit is checked for what of the list they carry, with how many. For a mineral short with a deposit known on the map, a suggestion marks the rock to mine: the nearest deposit the colony can walk up to, the cells nearest the way in first so each can be reached once the one before is mined, as many as the shortfall takes at the rock's yield and the best miner's, 40 at most a step, and no cell whose mining would leave a roof without a support within its reach. Undo takes the marks off what isn't mined yet; two days later the council checks that half of it was mined. Where Colony Manager's mining job mines the mineral, its target is raised instead.

li.heading: Fields by the weather
li.text: Each growing zone has a "By the weather" switch, off until you switch it on for a field. A field set to it sows only when sowing pays by the forecast: Rimfolk grows the field's crop hour by hour over the days ahead and works out how much of a full harvest a crop sown now would bring. Below 60% of a full harvest, sowing there pauses, and the field's own pane says why and when sowing is expected to pay again ("sowing paused, a frost in about 3 days would kill most of the young plants; worth sowing again in about 13 days"); at 60% or more it sows as usual and says what to expect and when it will be ripe. The 60% is a fixed line: a crop that would bring less is better sown a little later. Every other hour (and when the field's crop changes) it is worked out again.

points.li: The forecast is the game's own: the land's temperature for each hour ahead (its seasons, its days and nights and its run of warm and cold days, as the game itself reckons them), each condition on the map at its offset for as long as it lasts, and the weather's push on the temperature easing from what it is now. To be safe it is read 1 degree colder, and colder again by how much colder than the land's reckoning the real nights of the last 15 days got (1.5 degrees until 3 days are kept, at most 6).
Growth as the game grows plants: nothing from about 19:12 to 6:00, slowed by cold below the crop's optimal temperature and stopped below its least, slowed in poor light and by the field's soil.

Losses plant by plant: in 1.6 each plant dies at a cold limit of its own, between 10 and 18 degrees below the least temperature its crop grows at (so most crops die between -10 and -18 °C, not at a few degrees below freezing). Plants not yet sown are reckoned spread evenly over that range, or over the range the crop's plants on the map really have. A plant ripe enough to harvest when a killing frost comes counts as harvested early, at half its yield at the least growth to harvest up to all of it ripe; a plant that won't ripen in its life counts at what it gives then. Trees and other plants that only drop their leaves in the cold count as growing a day later, not as lost.

It only holds sowing back: the game's own season check still applies, a sowing you order by hand goes ahead, and harvesting is never held up. With Smart Farming (or ReGrowth's copy of it), leave a field set to sow by the weather on Smart Farming's "On" mode, so its own sowing check and early harvest don't work against this one.

li.heading: Harvest before a frost
li.text: For every outdoor growing zone, set to sow by the weather or not, the council looks 30 hours ahead each other hour. When the forecast falls below the cold limit of plants that are ripe enough to harvest, with 1 degree to spare, it suggests harvesting exactly those, with the numbers: "Frost tonight, about -12 °C around 3 at night: 9 of 37 rice plants in Growing zone 13 would die. Harvest the 9 now (about 60% of their full yield)?" It says too how many are too young to harvest and would die anyway, and how many should come through. Plants under a roof are never counted, and plants already marked to harvest or cut are left as they are. The suggestion comes as a message when it first appears, in the alerts while it stands (a click selects the field), as a button on the field, and among the suggestions on the Making page, ordered by the hours left. Harvest the 9 marks exactly those plants; Undo takes the marks off those not yet harvested; "Not this" sets that night's frost aside. A few hours after the coldest hour the council looks whether the frost came and how many of the plants were harvested in time, and says so under "Done lately". With "Harvest before a frost by itself" on (the default), the plants are marked as soon as the forecast shows the frost, without the click, and a message says so; Undo leaves that night's frost on that field to you.

li.heading: Your other mods
li.text: Bills set by Everybody Gets One ("one per person", "X per person", "with surplus"), and any bill whose repeat mode another mod added, are read but never changed. A bill Better Workbench Management links with others is changed together with every bill of its set, so the links stay as you made them. Better Pawn Control may set a work priority again when its presets switch. Anything another mod changes the ordinary way shows in the next hour's numbers.
